newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee up by 3.5 pct in new rally.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee up by 3.5 pct in new rally.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures, inspired by fresh rally in New York on Tuesday, scooped sharp gains on persistent speculative and trade buying to end Wednesday midsession some 3.5 percent up basis July.

The benchmark contract finished the morning trade at session's peak at $2,178 a tonne, up $76. But it fell short of the immediate technical upside target at $2,190 as origins stepped up offers into the advance.

Traders said a break above $2,190, the May 19 peak, could hold off some producer selling pressure and would allow the market another surge to the mid-$2,200s before selling creeps in again. Support is seen intact at $2,030.
This morning's producer selling into July widened July's discount to September to up $25 against $19 on Tuesday.
Volume was 3,940 lots, centred again on July and September.

New York arabica futures notched up nearly a seven percent gain on Tuesday on speculative-led buying on persistent supply concerns. The July contract hit a new life-high of 275.00 cents per lb before settling 17.45 cents up at 274.30.
Traders said that despite this morning's jump in London, the market continued to trail New York as robusta supplies were more readily available than arabicas.
"In New York, it's demand and no supply. Here...we do have some supplies," said one.
The market's main concern is the Brazilian weather as the country enters the dangerous frost months in June and July.

"There is no doubt that (arabica) coffee is physically tight with stockpiles in both consumer and producer countries near 20-year lows, and this makes the market extremely prone to weather scares in Brazil, even at this early stage of the season," broker GNI said. -- Jalil Hamid, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4985
